1:3.headline: God treads on the 'high places': mountains, or proud people?
1:3.body: God will tread on the במתי ארץ, the heights of the earth. Rashi reads these as the lofty and arrogant. Ibn Ezra knows that reading, of rulers, but says there is no need for it: God simply rules over all, even the mountains.

sources.quote: עַל הָרָמִים וְגַסֵּי הָרוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says it means on the high and the arrogant.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים: כי במתי ארץ - רמז לשליטים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read the heights of the earth as a hint to rulers.

sources.quote: ואין צורך, רק הטעם כי בכל מושל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says there is no need for that reading; the point is that God rules over everything.

1:4.headline: Melting mountains are a figure of speech for a nation's fall
1:4.body: The mountains melt like wax and the valleys split. Maimonides counts these among the prophets' well-known figures of speech, here for the fall of Samaria. Metzudat David reads the mountains as the leaders and the valleys as the common people.

sources.quote: ומיכה אמר על אובדן שומרון כשהוא משתמש והולך באמירות המליציות המפורסמות והידועות
sources.says: Maimonides says Micah spoke about the destruction of Samaria using well-known figures of speech.

sources.quote: ונמסו ההרים. הוא משל על השפלת השרים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the melting mountains are a figure for the humbling of the princes.

sources.quote: והעמקים יתבקעו. הוא משל על אבדן המון העם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the splitting valleys are a figure for the loss of the common people.

1:6.headline: Samaria turned into heaps of stone, or into pits?
1:6.body: Samaria will become לעי השדה. Rashi, Radak and the Targum read it as heaps, like the heap of stones Laban and Jacob set up. Ibn Ezra reads it as pits dug in a field.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ׳גַּלִּים׳ כְּמוֹ ״יְגַר שָׂהֲדוּתָא״
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for heaps, like 'the heap of witness' in Genesis 31.

sources.quote: כי הבנין החרב הוא גל אבנים
sources.says: Radak says it means heaps, because a ruined building becomes a heap of stones.

sources.quote: לעי - כמו לעיים חפירות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means pits dug in the ground.

1:7.headline: Idols named for the grief they bring
1:7.body: The idols here are called עצבים. Metzudat Zion says the name comes from עצב, sorrow: the idol grieves the one who serves it, because he calls and gets no answer.

sources.quote: העכו״ם תקרא כן על כי מעצבת לב עובדיה קורא ואינו נענה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says idols are called this because they grieve the heart of their worshipper, who calls and is not answered.

1:10.headline: Beth-le-Aphrah, roll in the dust (עפר)
1:10.body: The town עפרה is told to roll in עפר, dust. Rashi calls it a play on words, and says all the towns here are mourned by their names. Radak adds that the town's name is even voiced differently here to sound closer to עפר.

sources.quote: כֻּלָּם לְפִי שֵׁם הָעִיר לְשׁוֹן הַקִּינָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a play of words, and every one of these lament lines follows the name of the town.

sources.quote: לפיכך נראה שקרא לעפרה בפתח העי"ן לקרב יותר הקריאה לקריאת עפר
sources.says: Radak says the name is read with a different vowel here to bring it closer to the sound of עפר, dust.

sources.quote: והוא לשון הנופל על לשון עפרה שמה ובעפר התגלגלי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a play on words: Aphrah is its name, so roll in dust.

1:11.headline: 'Shaphir', the pretty town, goes out naked and shamed
1:11.body: שפיר means beautiful, and Radak says the verse turns that beauty into the ugliness of nakedness. Rashi and Metzudat David hear another play: שפיר is also a word for what comes out of a woman's womb.

sources.quote: כי שפיר היא יופי ונוי
sources.says: Radak says שפיר means beauty and loveliness, and the verse reverses it into shameful nakedness.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר נִקְרֵאת שָׁפִיר שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם נֵפֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מֵרַחְמָהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it is called Shaphir, which is the name for a stillborn that comes out of a woman's womb, and so it goes out uncovered in shame.

sources.quote: וגם הוא לשון נופל על לשון כי שפיר הוא ענין שליא
sources.says: Metzudat David says this too is a play on words, since שפיר means the afterbirth.

1:11.headline: The people of Zaanan did not 'go out' (יצאה)
1:11.body: Zaanan's people לא יצאה, did not go out to mourn. Radak and Metzudat David point out that יצאה and צאנן sound alike. Radak says they stayed home because they knew their own exile was coming.

sources.quote: גם זה לשון נופל על הלשון כי יצאה וצאנן קרובים בלשון
sources.says: Radak says this too is a play on words, since 'went out' and Zaanan sound close.

sources.quote: וגם זה לשון הנופל על לשון כי יצאה וצאנן קרובים בלשון
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a play on words, as 'went out' and Zaanan are close in sound.

1:11.headline: Beth-ha-Ezel, the 'house next door'
1:11.body: אצל means beside. Rashi reads the town's name as a charge: they took their neighbors' land, house beside house, field beside field. The mourning they caused will take away the buildings they set up there.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי לְהַגִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבַיִת שָׂדֶה בְּשָׂדֶה זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says they robbed others' land to join house to house and field to field, one beside the other.

sources.quote: הוּא יִקַּח מִכֶּם עֲמָדְתוֹ מַעֲמַד הַבִּנְיָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says the mourning they caused will take from them the buildings they put up on that land.

1:12.headline: Maroth: just a town, or the town that 'rebelled'?
1:12.body: Ibn Ezra says מרות is simply a town's name. Others hear מרי, rebellion, in it. Malbim reads it that way, and Rashi says the town defied the prophets yet hoped for good.

sources.quote: כי, מרות - שם עיר. ויש אומרים: מגזרת תרגום: מרי שמיא או מגזרת מרי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Maroth is a town's name, and some derive it from מרי, but he finds that reading has no basis.

sources.quote: ומרות. מענין מרי ומרידה
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from rebellion.

sources.quote: אוֹתָהּ הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּשַׁלְוָתָהּ וּמַמְרָה עַל פִּי הַנְּבִיאִים
sources.says: Rashi says the town sat at ease and defied the word of the prophets.

1:15.headline: Mareshah will get a new heir (יורש)
1:15.body: God will bring an heir, יורש, a conqueror, to מרשה. Rashi and Radak call it a play on words. Ibn Ezra adds that Micah himself may have come from this town.

sources.quote: יוֹרֵשׁ לְמָרֵשָׁה לָשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל הַלָּשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says 'heir' for Mareshah is a play on words.

sources.quote: גם זה לשון נופל על הלשון כי יורש ומרשה קרובים בלשון
sources.says: Radak says this too is a play on words, since יורש and מרשה sound close.

sources.quote: ויתכן: שזה הנביא היה מזאת העיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be that this prophet came from this town.

1:16.headline: Make yourself bald as an eagle: why an eagle?
1:16.body: The land is told to shave its head bald like a נשר in mourning. Rashi, with the Targum, says the eagle sheds many of its feathers. Radak repeats a belief that once in ten years the eagle flies so near the heat above that its feathers fall out.

sources.quote: דֶּרֶךְ הַנֶּשֶׁר לִמְרֹט רוֹב כְּנָפָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is the eagle's way to shed most of its feathers.

sources.quote: ואחת לעשר שנים יעוף מאד למעלה עד האויר העליון הסמוך לגלגל האש ומרוב חומו ימרטו כנפיו
sources.says: Radak says once every ten years the eagle flies very high, near the sphere of fire, and from the heat its feathers fall off.

2:4.headline: One odd spelling says both 'we were robbed' and 'they robbed us'
2:4.body: Rashi notes that נשדנו is spelled so it points two ways at once, to the victims and to the robbers. He also gives another reading: we brought this robbery on ourselves.

sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּא לְשַׁמֵּשׁ שְׁנֵי לְשׁוֹנוֹת, לְשׁוֹן נִפְעַלְנוּ וְלָשׁוֹן פְּעַלְנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the word is written to serve two forms at once, 'we were done to' and 'they did to us'.

sources.quote: דָּבָר אַחֵר נְשַׁדֻּנוּ אֲנַחְנוּ גָּרַמְנוּ לְעַצְמֵנוּ שֶׁשְּׁדָדוּנוּ
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: we ourselves caused them to rob us.

2:6.headline: 'Do not drip': the word for dripping also means preaching
2:6.body: The people tell the prophets אל תטפו, literally 'do not drip'. The commentators explain that dripping is borrowed for prophecy, speech that flows out like drops.

sources.quote: כָּל טִיף לְשׁוֹן ׳נְבוּאָה׳
sources.says: Rashi says every use of this verb means prophecy, as in Amos and Ezekiel.

sources.quote: הוא מל׳ נטיפה והזלה והושאל בענין הדבור של נבואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means dripping and flowing, borrowed for the speech of prophecy.

sources.quote: ענין הזלת הדבור כמו ועלימו תטיף מלתי
sources.says: Radak says it means flowing speech, as in 'my word dropped upon them'.

2:6.headline: Will shame overtake them, or never go away?
2:6.body: Ibn Ezra reads יסג as if it were 'overtake': whoever stops preaching to them will not be shamed. Malbim takes it from 'to turn back': the disgrace of their deeds will never leave them.

sources.quote: ובא על משקל קל תחת כבד, לומר ישג במקום ישיג, כי מי שלא יטיף למשפחה הזאת, לא תשיגנו כלימה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word stands for 'overtake': a prophet who does not preach to this family will not be overtaken by shame.

sources.quote: כלימות אשר לא יוסג ויופרש מהם, כמו ולא נסוג ממך
sources.says: Malbim reads it as disgrace that will not turn back and part from them.

2:7.headline: A question, or 'you who are called House of Jacob'?
2:7.body: Rashi reads האמור as a question: is this what the House of Jacob says? Radak, and Rabbi Yeshua as cited by Ibn Ezra, read it as an address: 'you who are called the House of Jacob'.

sources.quote: הֲזֹאת יֹאמְרוּ בֵּית יַעֲקֹב
sources.says: Rashi reads it as a question: is this what the House of Jacob will say?

sources.quote: ורבי ישועה אמר: כאילו כתב שמע אתה הקרוא בית יעקב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Yeshua: it is as if it said 'hear, you who are called House of Jacob'.

sources.quote: כלומר אתה שאומרים לך בית יעקב
sources.says: Radak says it means 'you who are called House of Jacob'.

2:7.headline: Is God's spirit short: his will, his prophecy, or his patience?
2:7.body: The people ask הקצר רוח ה', 'is the LORD's spirit short?'. Metzudat David reads spirit as will, Ibn Ezra as prophecy, and Malbim as patience, like a short-tempered person.

sources.quote: וכי קצר רצון ה׳ לבל יוכל למלאותו להיטיב למי שירצה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as: is God's will too short to carry out good for whom He wishes?

sources.quote: הקצר רוח ה' - היא הנבואה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the spirit here is prophecy.

sources.quote: קצר רוח. מי שאינו מושל ברוחו
sources.says: Malbim says 'short of spirit' means someone who cannot rule his own temper.

2:12.headline: Sheep of Bozrah, or sheep in a walled fold?
2:12.body: Radak reads בצרה as Bozrah, a large city of Edom rich in flocks. Rashi and Metzudat Zion hear the word for a fortress: sheep packed safely in a walled pen.

sources.quote: כצאן בצרה. עיר גדולה מאדום והיא ארץ מקנה ומקנה רב בה
sources.says: Radak says Bozrah is a large city of Edom, a land of many flocks.

sources.quote: כְּצֹאן רַבָּה הַנְּתוּנָה בְּמִבְצְרֵי גִּדְרוֹת צֹאן
sources.says: Rashi says it means a large flock placed in the walled enclosures of sheepfolds.

sources.quote: בלשון שאלה אמר על דיר הצאן שהיא להם למבצר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is borrowed for a sheep pen, which is the flock's fortress.

2:13.headline: Who is 'the one who breaks through'?
2:13.body: The midrash cited by Radak says the breaker is Elijah, clearing the way for the Messiah. Radak also records a reading about King Zedekiah fleeing through a breach, and Malbim sees a wicked king who breaks down the law.

sources.quote: ובדרש הפורץ זה אליהו מלכם זה צמח בן דוד
sources.says: Radak cites the midrash: the breaker is Elijah, and their king is the Messiah, son of David.

sources.quote: על צדקיהו כשיצא דרך בין החומותים שפרצו לפניו החומה
sources.says: Radak cites his father's reading: it is Zedekiah, who escaped between the walls through a breach made for him.

sources.quote: שהוא המלך הפורץ גדר ומפר דת והורס חומותיה
sources.says: Malbim says it is a king who breaks the fence, overturns the law and tears down its walls.

4:1.headline: ונהרו: the nations will 'stream' like a river to the mountain
4:1.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra tie ונהרו to the word נהר, a river, because it runs. Rashi says the nations gather there like rivers flowing to the sea, and Metzudat Zion says they will be drawn like a river.

sources.quote: וירוצו ומזה נקרא מרוצת המים הרבים נהר
sources.says: Radak says they will run, and from this the running of many waters is called a river.

sources.quote: ירוצו מגזרת נהר, כי הוא רץ לעולם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they will run, from the word for river, since it always runs.

sources.quote: וְנִקְבְּצוּ שָׁם יַחַד כַּנְּהָרוֹת הַהוֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם
sources.says: Rashi says they will gather there together like the rivers going to the sea.

sources.quote: ימשכו כנהר וכן ונהרו אל טוב ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they will be drawn like a river, as in 'they shall stream to the Lord's goodness'.

4:2.headline: 'He will teach us': God, or King Messiah?
4:2.body: Metzudat David says God teaches us through those who know the Torah. Radak says the teacher is King Messiah, of whom the next verse says 'he will judge'.

sources.quote: המקום ילמד אותנו ע״י יודעי התורה
sources.says: Metzudat David says God will teach us through those who know the Torah.

sources.quote: והמורה הוא מלך המשיח ועליו אמר ושפט
sources.says: Radak says the teacher is King Messiah, of whom it says 'and he shall judge'.

4:2.headline: 'His ways' and 'His paths': the big principles and the details
4:2.body: Malbim says מדרכיו are the great roots of true religion, and ארחתיו the small details they will then walk in by themselves. Metzudat David reads מדרכיו as 'some of His ways'.

sources.quote: ויורנו מדרכיו הגדולים, ונלכה מעצמנו בארחותיו הפרטים
sources.says: Malbim says He will teach us His great ways, and we will walk on our own in His particular paths.

sources.quote: מדרכיו. מה מדרכיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says מדרכיו means 'some of His ways'.

4:3.headline: Who is the judge? The Messiah, God's word, or Jerusalem's people?
4:3.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra say the judge is King Messiah, while Ibn Ezra also reports the view that it is God and His word, or the people of Jerusalem. Rashi says ושפט here means rebuke.

sources.quote: השופט הוא מלך המשיח
sources.says: Radak says the judge is King Messiah.

sources.quote: ושפט - השופט הוא המשיח. ויפת אמר: השם הנכבד ודבר ה'. ואחרים אמרו: אנשי ירושלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the judge is the Messiah, then reports Yefet, 'the Honored Name and the word of the Lord', and others, 'the people of Jerusalem'.

sources.quote: מִשְׁפָּט זֶה לְשׁוֹן ׳תּוֹכָחָה׳ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says this משפט means rebuke.

4:4.headline: 'The Lord has spoken': Rashi points to the verse where He did
4:4.body: Rashi asks where God spoke this and answers: 'I will give peace in the land', in Leviticus. The Targum says the Lord decreed it by His word.

sources.quote: וְהֵיכָן דִּבֵּר ״וְנָתַתִּי שָׁלוֹם בָּאָרֶץ״
sources.says: Rashi asks where He spoke, and answers 'I will give peace in the land'.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי בְּמֵימְרָא דַייָ צְבָאוֹת גְזַר כֵּן
sources.says: The Targum says that by the word of the Lord of hosts He decreed it so.

4:6.headline: 'I will gather the lame': gather, or heal?
4:6.body: Rashi says that אספה may mean 'heal', like 'he would heal him of his leprosy' in 2 Kings. Malbim says אסף means bringing in from outside, while קבץ means gathering the scattered.

sources.quote: וְלִי נִרְאֶה לְשׁוֹן ׳מַרְפֵּא׳ כְּמוֹ ״וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ מִצָּרַעְתּוֹ״
sources.says: Rashi says it seems to him to be a language of healing, like 'and he will heal him of his leprosy'.

sources.quote: שפעל אסף עקרו על הכנסת איזה דבר מן החוץ אל הפנים, ופעל קבץ בא על קיבוץ המפוזרות
sources.says: Malbim says the verb אסף is at root about bringing something in from outside, and קבץ is for gathering what is scattered.

sources.quote: אספה. כמו אאספה
sources.says: Radak says אספה is like אאספה, 'I will gather'.

4:6.headline: 'The lame one': limping, wandering, or hidden in a corner?
4:6.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak read הצולעה as the limping, those in pain in exile. The Targum renders it 'the wanderers', and Malbim also reads it as צלע, 'a side', for a people hidden in a far corner of the earth.

sources.quote: הצולעה. החגרת כמו והוא צולע על ירכו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הצולעה is the limping one, like 'and he limped on his thigh'.

sources.quote: ופירוש הצולעה ישראל שהם בגלות כחולים והצולעים וכואבים
sources.says: Radak says הצולעה is Israel, who in exile are like the sick, the limping and the aching.

sources.quote: אֶכְנוֹשׁ מְטַלְטְלַיָא וּמְבַדְרַיָא
sources.says: The Targum says 'I will gather the wanderers and the scattered'.

sources.quote: או מענין צלע וזויות על שנחבאים כל ימי הגלות בצלע כדור הארץ
sources.says: Malbim says or from the sense of a side or corner, because they are hidden all the days of exile in the side of the earth.

4:6.headline: 'The lame' and 'the driven': one people or two?
4:6.body: Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra read both words as the same people, Israel, said twice. Malbim reads them as two groups: the ten tribes, pushed out to a far land, and Judah, scattered everywhere.

sources.quote: ישראל הנדחה מארצה לארצות העכו״ם
sources.says: Metzudat David says Israel, driven from its land to the lands of the nations.

sources.quote: ביום, הצולעה - מישראל שלא תוכל ללכת במהרה וככה: הנדחה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the lame is of Israel, who cannot walk quickly, and the same goes for the driven.

sources.quote: ישראל שהם עשרת השבטים לא נפוצו בפיזור גדול בין העמים רק נדחו ממקומם
sources.says: Malbim says the ten tribes were not scattered widely among the nations but were pushed out of their place.

sources.quote: ושבט יהודה הם נפוצו לארבע רוחות השמים וצריכים קיבוץ
sources.says: Malbim says the tribe of Judah was scattered to the four winds and needs gathering.

4:7.headline: והנהלאה: 'far removed', 'worn out', or 'strong and ahead'?
4:7.body: This word appears only here. Ibn Ezra and Malbim derive it from הלאה, 'far', Metzudat Zion from the word for weariness, and Radak's father read it as the strong, fat sheep that walks ahead of the flock.

sources.quote: מגזרת הלאה ולא מתלאה, כי תלאה שורשו תלא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from הלאה, 'further', not from תלאה, 'hardship', since that root is תלא.

sources.quote: נגזר ממלת גש הלאה שמורה על התרחקות
sources.says: Malbim says it is derived from the words 'draw further', which point to going far away.

sources.quote: והנהלאה. ענין יגיעה כמו נלאה מואב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says והנהלאה means weariness, like 'Moab is weary'.

sources.quote: הנהלאה החזקה והשמנה ההולכת מהלאה לפני הצאן מרוב בריאותה
sources.says: Radak gives his father's reading: the strong and fat one, who goes ahead of the flock out of her health.

4:8.headline: מגדל עדר: Zion, David's tower, a place near Bethlehem, or the Messiah?
4:8.body: Ibn Ezra says it is Jerusalem, a tower for the flock of Israel, and Radak says it is David's tower. Malbim says Migdal Eder is a place near Bethlehem, and the Targum has 'you, Messiah of Israel, hidden because of the sins of Zion'.

sources.quote: והנכון: ירושלם, שהוא כמגדל לעדר שהם ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is Jerusalem, which is like a tower for the flock, who are Israel.

sources.quote: הוא מגדל דוד וקראו מגדל עדר כי ישראל נמשלים לעדר הצאן
sources.says: Radak says it is David's tower, called the tower of the flock because Israel is likened to a flock of sheep.

sources.quote: מגדל עדר. שם מקום סמוך לבית לחם אפרתה
sources.says: Malbim says מגדל עדר is the name of a place near Bethlehem Ephrathah.

sources.quote: וְאַתְּ מְשִׁיחָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל דְטָמִיר מִן קֳדָם חוֹבֵי כְנִשְׁתָּא דְצִיוֹן
sources.says: The Targum says 'you, the Messiah of Israel, who is hidden because of the sins of the congregation of Zion'.

4:8.headline: עפל: a fortress hill, or 'hidden' from אפל, 'dark'?
4:8.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read עפל as a tower or fortress, like עופל ובחן in Isaiah. Rashi says the Targum renders it 'hidden', from אפל, darkness.

sources.quote: עופל. ענין מגדל ומבצר כמו עופל ובחן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עופל means a tower and fortress, like 'Ophel and the watchtower'.

sources.quote: עופל - כמו: עופל ובחן. ויש אומרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עופל is like 'Ophel and the watchtower', and then gives another view.

sources.quote: וְתִרְגֵּם עֹפֶל לְשׁוֹן ׳אֹפֶל׳
sources.says: Rashi says Jonathan translated עפל as the language of darkness, אפל.

sources.quote: תרגם עופל טמיר כמו שתרגם
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translated עופל as 'hidden', as he did elsewhere.

4:9.headline: 'Is there no king in you?': God, or a human king?
4:9.body: Radak and Metzudat David say the king is God, your king and counselor. Malbim and the Targum read it as a human king: you still have a king and counselors, so why this panic?

sources.quote: הלא מלכך ויועצך האל יתברך
sources.says: Radak says surely your king and counselor is God.

sources.quote: וכי אין בך המלך ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says is not the Lord the King in you?

sources.quote: הלא עתה עדיין יש בך מלך ויועצים
sources.says: Malbim says now you still have a king and counselors in you.

sources.quote: הֲמַלְכָּא לֵית בִּיךְ אִם מַלְכֵי מַלְכֵּךְ אֲבָדוּ
sources.says: The Targum asks: is there no king in you, or have the kings of your kingdom perished?

4:10.headline: 'There you will be saved': or 'there you will be emptied'?
4:10.body: The Targum and Malbim read תנצלי as rescued: the exiles of Babylon were saved. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it as stripped and emptied, like 'they stripped themselves of their ornaments' in Exodus.

sources.quote: תַּמָן תִּישְׁתֵּיזְבִין
sources.says: The Targum says 'there you will be saved'.

sources.quote: רק גולי בבל נצולו
sources.says: Malbim says only the exiles of Babylon were saved.

sources.quote: תנצלי. ענין ריקות כמו ויתנצלו בני ישראל את עדים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תנצלי means emptiness, like 'and the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments'.

sources.quote: בבבל תתרוקני מכל הטובה ולא יועילו לך מלכי מצרים
sources.says: Metzudat David says in Babylon you will be emptied of all good, and the kings of Egypt will not help you.

4:11.headline: 'May Zion be defiled': guilty, or made to flatter?
4:11.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read תחנף as Zion becoming guilty, like 'do not pollute the land' in Numbers. Malbim reads it as Zion cringing and serving them, like a servant who flatters his master.

sources.quote: עַתָּה תִּתְחַיֵּב צִיּוֹן בְּחַטֹּאתֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says now Zion will be found guilty in her sins.

sources.quote: תחנף. תתחייב כמו ולא תחניפו את הארץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תחנף means will be found guilty, like 'and you shall not pollute the land'.

sources.quote: שתהיה נכנעת ומשועבדת להם, כעבד החונף לאדוניו
sources.says: Malbim says that she will be submissive and enslaved to them, like a servant who flatters his master.

sources.quote: שיחניפו לציון כאילו באו לחסות בצל קדושתה
sources.says: Malbim says another reading is that they would flatter Zion, as if they came to shelter in the shade of her holiness.

4:12.headline: 'Thoughts' and 'plan': God's means and His goal
4:12.body: Malbim says מחשבות are the steps God takes and עצה is the goal they lead to, and ידע is knowing what the senses show while הבין is grasping it with the mind. The Targum renders מחשבות as 'secrets'.

sources.quote: עצת ה' הוא התכלית הנרצה אליו במעשהו, והמחשבות הם האמצעיים
sources.says: Malbim says God's plan is the goal He wants in what He does, and the thoughts are the means.

sources.quote: ויש הבדל בין ידיעה להבנה, שהידיעה תפול על דבר המושג בחוש, וההבנה על דבר המושג בשכלו
sources.says: Malbim says there is a difference between knowing and understanding: knowing is of what is grasped by the senses, and understanding of what is grasped by the mind.

sources.quote: וְאִינוּן לָא יָדְעִין רָזַיָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum says they do not know the secrets of the Lord.

4:13.headline: בצעם: ill-gotten gain, or simply their wealth?
4:13.body: Rashi says it means what they gathered by robbery and violence, and Malbim says it is money mostly earned unjustly. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra read it as plain wealth, like הונם.

sources.quote: מַה שֶּׁכִּנְּסוּ מִגְּזֵלָה וְחָמָס
sources.says: Rashi says it is what they gathered from robbery and violence.

sources.quote: בצע מיוחד על ממון שהרויח ורובו שלא במשפט
sources.says: Malbim says בצע is specially for money a person gained, mostly not by justice.

sources.quote: בצעם. חמדת עשרם כמו בצע כסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says בצעם is the desire of their riches, like 'a gain of silver'.

sources.quote: בצעם - כמו בצע. והטעם כמו הונם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בצעם is like בצע, and means the same as 'their wealth'.

6:1.headline: Plead before the mountains: the fathers of the nation
6:1.body: God tells the prophet to argue His case before the mountains and hills. Rashi reads the mountains as the patriarchs and the hills as the matriarchs, and Radak says Targum Jonathan read it that way too, so the ancestors hear what their children did.

sources.quote: אֶת הֶהָרִים. אֶת הָאָבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says "the mountains" means the patriarchs.

sources.quote: הַגְּבָעוֹת. הָאִמָּהוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says "the hills" means the matriarchs.

sources.quote: וי"ת ההרים אבהתא והגבעות אמהתא כלומר שישמעו האבות שהם אברהם יצחק ויעקב
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translated the mountains as the fathers and the hills as the mothers, so that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob would hear.

6:3.headline: "How have I wearied you?" Maimonides: the Torah lightens the load
6:3.body: God asks what burden He ever put on Israel. Maimonides quotes this verse to show that the Torah's worship is light compared with the cruel rites of other nations, such as burning children.

sources.quote: באה רק להקל את עבודות האל ולהפחית את הטורח
sources.says: Maimonides says the Torah came only to make the worship of God lighter and to reduce the burden, and he cites this verse as proof.

sources.quote: מה דבר בקשתי מאתך שתלאה לעשותו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God asks: what did I ask of you that was too tiring to do?

sources.quote: וּמָה הֶלְאֵתִיךָ. בַּעֲבוֹדָתִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means: how did I weary you with My service?

6:4.headline: Three leaders sent ahead, and Miriam taught the women
6:4.body: Targum Jonathan gives each of the three a task: Moses to teach the law, Aaron to atone for the people, and Miriam to teach the women. Ibn Ezra also says Miriam prophesied to the women.

sources.quote: מֹשֶׁה לְאַלָפָא מְסִירַת דִינִין אַהֲרֹן לְכַפָּרָא עַל עַמָא וּמִרְיָם לְאוֹרָאָה לִנְשַׁיָא
sources.says: The Targum says Moses was sent to teach the laws, Aaron to atone for the people, and Miriam to instruct the women.

sources.quote: ומרים - שהתנבאה לנשים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Miriam prophesied to the women.

6:8.headline: Walk humbly: some things God wants done quietly
6:8.body: הצנע is found only here and means modest or hidden. Rashi says God, unlike a person, wants a quiet return and not a public apology, and Radak brings the sages, who say even public acts like funerals and weddings call for modesty.

sources.quote: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵין חָפֵץ אֶלָּא שֶׁיָּשׁוּב אֵלָיו בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God wants only that a person return to Him privately, between himself and God.

sources.quote: והצנע לכת עם אלהיך זה הוצאת המת והכנסת כלה
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: "walk humbly with your God" refers to escorting the dead and bringing in a bride.

sources.quote: ואמר והצנע כי הדבר הזה מסור ללב והוא דבר צניעות
sources.says: Radak says it says "humbly" because loving God is a matter of the heart, something private.

6:9.headline: Tushiyah, wisdom, named for "being" because it lasts forever
6:9.body: תושיה means sound wisdom, the wisdom of Torah. Metzudat Zion and Radak tie it to יש, "there is", because it stays in being forever while everything else passes away.

sources.quote: ותושיה הוא ענין חכמת התורה והוא מלשון יש כי ישנה לעולם ולא תשוב לאין כיתר הדברים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says tushiyah is the wisdom of Torah, from the word יש, because it exists forever and does not return to nothing like other things.

sources.quote: מענין יש כי אין בעולם השפל דבר עומד אלא היא
sources.says: Radak says it comes from יש, because nothing in this lower world lasts except wisdom.

6:9.headline: Yir'eh: Malbim hears the name Abraham gave Jerusalem
6:9.body: Abraham named the mountain of the binding "God will see", יראה. Malbim reads this verse as calling Jerusalem by that name, to remind it that God's eyes are always on it.

sources.quote: וכונתו עמ"ש ויקרא אברהם שם המקום ההוא ה' יראה, שתחלה היתה נקראת בשם שלם
sources.says: Malbim says the verse points to Abraham naming the place "God will see", when the city was first called Shalem.

sources.quote: כי כבר היה שם העיר שלם והוסיף יראה
sources.says: Malbim says the city already had the name Shalem, and Yir'eh was added to it.

6:10.headline: A "lean" measure, or one set by the officials?
6:10.body: Rashi reads איפת רזון as a short measure the rich use to cheat the poor and make them thin. Malbim reads רזון as one of the רוזנים, the officials who fix the measures, so even the official measure is crooked.

sources.quote: מִדָּה קְטַנָּה שֶׁעֲשִׁירֵיכֶם מְרַמִּים בָּהּ הָעֲנִיִּים וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתָן לִידֵי רָזוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it is a small measure your rich use to cheat the poor, bringing them to leanness.

sources.quote: רזון. יחיד משם רוזנים
sources.says: Malbim says רזון is the singular of רוזנים, officials.

sources.quote: זו היא איפה קטנה שהיא רזה וחסרה
sources.says: Radak says it is a small measure, thin and short.

6:13.headline: Measure for measure: you made the poor sick, so I strike you
6:13.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra read החליתי as a matching punishment. Just as the cheaters wore down the poor and oppressed, God now strikes them with a hard blow.

sources.quote: כמו שאתה החלית העניים והעשוקים במרמותיך כן אני החליתי אותך בהכות אותך מכה קשה
sources.says: Radak says: as you made the poor and oppressed sick with your cheating, so I made you sick by striking you hard.

sources.quote: אם אתה עשית חמס והחלית לבב עשוקים, גם אני החליתיך עת הכיתיך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says: if you did violence and sickened the hearts of the oppressed, I too sickened you when I struck you.

6:14.headline: A sickness that bends you over, or being brought low?
6:14.body: וישחך is found only here. Rashi, following the Sifre and Targum Jonathan, reads it as a curse in the belly that makes you sick and bent over, while Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as being humbled.

sources.quote: וְיִגְרוֹם לְךָ חֹלִי שֶׁתְּהֵא חוֹלֶה וְהוֹלֵךְ שָׁחוֹחַ
sources.says: Rashi says the food will cause you an illness so that you go about sick and bent over.

sources.quote: וישחך. ענין שפלות והכנעה כמו וישח אדם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lowliness and humbling, as in "man is bowed down".

sources.quote: הכנעתך תהיה בקרבך
sources.says: Radak says your humbling will be within you.

6:14.headline: Overtake the captors, or conceive and not give birth?
6:14.body: Rashi reads ותסג as catching up with the enemy who carries off your children, yet failing to rescue them. Radak and Ibn Ezra read it as a woman who conceives but cannot deliver.

sources.quote: וְתַסֵּג. אֶת אוֹיְבֶיךָ הַמּוֹלִיכִים בָּנֶיךָ וּבְנוֹתֶיךָ בַּשְּׁבִי וְלֹא תְפַלְּטֵם
sources.says: Rashi says you will overtake the enemies taking your sons and daughters captive, and not rescue them.

sources.quote: תסיג האשה להריון ולא תפליט הולד
sources.says: Radak says the woman will conceive but will not deliver the child.

sources.quote: תשיג אל הריון ולא תלד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says your wife will conceive and not give birth.

6:15.headline: Treading "new wine"? Grapes, named for what they become
6:15.body: The verse says you will tread תירוש, new wine. Radak notes that one treads grapes, not wine, and says they are called by what they will become, like "grinding flour".

sources.quote: ותירוש. על שם סופו כמו וטחני קמח כי לא ידרוך האדם התירוש אלא הענבים
sources.says: Radak says it is named for its end, like "grinding flour", since a person treads grapes, not wine.

sources.quote: תדרוך את ענבי היין
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means you will tread the wine grapes.

7:1.headline: Not "summer gatherers" but the last poor figs of summer
7:1.body: Rashi says the vowels show this is not "gatherers" but "the gathering": the poor figs left at the end of summer. Radak says the prophet is like the little that remains after the harvest.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן פּוֹעֵל כְּמוֹ ׳יוֹשֵׁב׳ אוֹמֵר אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן מִפְעָל
sources.says: Rashi says the word is not a verb form like יושב but a noun.

sources.quote: כַּאֲסִיפַת קַיִץ וְהֵם סוֹפֵי תְאֵנִים שֶׁהֵן רָעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it means the summer gathering, the last figs, which are poor.

sources.quote: נשארתי בדבר מועט הנשאר אחר שלקטו ואספו פירות הקיץ
sources.says: Radak says the prophet is left like the little that remains after the summer fruit is picked.

7:1.headline: No cluster to eat: no one who has everything in him
7:1.body: The Targum and Rashi read the grape cluster as a person with good deeds, and there is none left. Malbim cites the Rabbis, who hear in אשכול the words איש שהכל בו, "a man who has everything in him".

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ ״לֵית גְּבַר דְּבֵיהּ עוֹבָדִין טָבִין״
sources.says: Rashi follows the Targum: there is no man with good deeds.

sources.quote: כלומר אין חסיד וישר שאלמוד מעשיו
sources.says: Radak says it means there is no pious, upright man whose deeds I could learn from.

sources.quote: וכמ"ש חז"ל אשכול איש שהכל בו
sources.says: Malbim cites the Rabbis: אשכול is a man who has everything in him.

7:2.headline: חרם: a hunter's net, or handing over to destruction
7:2.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read חרם as a net, as in Ezekiel 26:5: each man hunts his brother like a bird. The Targum reads it as destruction: they hand each other over to be wiped out.

sources.quote: חרם. רשת כמו משטח חרמים
sources.says: Radak says חרם is a net, as in "a place for spreading nets".

sources.quote: חרם. כמו בחרם והוא הרשת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says חרם means with a net.

sources.quote: מָסְרִין לִגְמִירָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it "they hand over to destruction".

7:3.headline: Three corrupt officials braid injustice like a three-strand rope
7:3.body: עבות is a thick rope. Rashi and Radak say such a rope has three strands, and the verse names three men: the official, the judge and the great one. Together they twist the crooked ruling tight.

sources.quote: עֲשָׂאוּהָ קְלִיעָה שֶׁל חֵטְא בֵּין שְׁלָשְׁתָּן
sources.says: Rashi says the three of them made it a braid of sin.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָעֲבוֹת מְשֻׁלֶּשֶׁת הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says a rope is made of three strands.

sources.quote: וכן אמר ויעבתוה לפי שהם שלשה מחזיקי העולה והטיית הדין השר והשופט והגדול
sources.says: Radak says the verse uses this word because three men hold up the wrong and the bent judgment: the official, the judge and the great one.

sources.quote: יעשו עבות שהיא משלשה מיתרים כמ"ש חז"ל
sources.says: Malbim says they make a rope of three strands, as the Rabbis said.

7:3.headline: Doing evil "well": a word set against its opposite
7:3.body: The verse puts רע, "evil", beside היטיב, "do well". Radak calls this an elegant turn of speech that sets a word against its opposite, as in I Samuel 20:13. Metzudat Zion says it means they do evil thoroughly.

sources.quote: וזה דרך צחות לומר לשון על הפכו לענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says it is an elegant way of speech, using a word together with its opposite for one idea.

sources.quote: להיטיב. ענין חוזק כמו ההיטיב חרה לך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says להיטיב means strength, as in Jonah 4:4.

sources.quote: עַל שְׂכַר הָרָעַת כַּפֵּיכֶם אַתֶּם מְקַוִּים שֶׁיֵּיטִיב לָכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they hope the evil of their hands will be rewarded with good.

7:4.headline: Their straightest man: worse than a thorn hedge, or straight only beside one
7:4.body: Rashi and Radak read: the most upright of them is worse than a hedge of thorns. Malbim reads: a briar is crooked, but looks straight next to a tangled hedge. So their best man is straight only compared with his crooked generation.

sources.quote: יָשָׁר שֶׁבָּהֶם רַע מִמְּסוּכַת קוֹצִים
sources.says: Rashi says the upright one among them is worse than a hedge of thorns.

sources.quote: והישר שבהם הוא קשה יותר מן המסוכה שהוא גדר הכרמים שעושים מקוצים
sources.says: Radak says the upright one among them is harsher than the thorn hedge built around vineyards.

sources.quote: עד שהחדק הוא ישר בערכו, וכן הטוב שבהם הוא ג"כ נפתל ועקש, רק שהוא ישר בערך בני דורו
sources.says: Malbim says the briar is straight only by comparison, and so the good man among them is also crooked, straight only next to his generation.

7:4.headline: מצפיך: the day you hoped for, or the day your watchmen promised
7:4.body: Rashi reads it as the day you waited for, hoping for good, which brings punishment instead. Radak reads מצפיך as your lookouts: the false prophets who promised you lies. Malbim reads them as the nations watching for your fall.

sources.quote: יוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מְצַפֶּה בּוֹ לְטוֹבָה תָּבֹא פְּקֻדָּתְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the day you hope will be good is the day your punishment comes.

sources.quote: יום נביאי השקר שהם מצפיך ונביאיך שהיו מבטיחים אותך על שקר
sources.says: Radak says it is the day of the false prophets, your watchmen, who made you false promises.

sources.quote: ר"ל על האומות שמצפים לראות ברעתך
sources.says: Malbim says it refers to the nations that wait to see your harm.

7:5.headline: "Do not trust a friend": the Rabbis read the Friend as God
7:5.body: Plainly, the verse warns that in this generation no friend can be trusted. Rashi brings the Rabbis' reading: do not sin while saying God is our friend and will forgive us.

sources.quote: בדור הזה אין אדם יכול להאמין ברעו
sources.says: Radak says in this generation no one can trust his friend.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה אַל תֶּחֱטָאוּ וְתֹאמְרוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹהֲבֵנוּ וְהוּא יִמְחוֹל לָנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the Rabbis read it about God: do not sin and say the Holy One loves us and will forgive us.

7:5.headline: "She who lies in your arms": your wife, or your own soul
7:5.body: Radak and Metzudat David read it as a man's wife: even with her, guard your words. Rashi reads it as your own soul, which will testify against you.

sources.quote: גם מאשתך צריך אתה שתשמור פתחי פיך
sources.says: Radak says you must guard your words even from your wife.

sources.quote: מאשתך השוכבת בחיקך
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means your wife who lies in your arms.

sources.quote: נִשְׁמָתְךָ הִיא תָּעִיד בְּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it is your soul, which will testify against you.

7:11.headline: ירחק חק: the set time is far off, or the decree is lifted
7:11.body: Rashi first reads it as the enemy's taunt: the day you wait for keeps being pushed back. His second reading, shared by Ibn Ezra, is good news: the foreign decrees and taxes will be removed.

sources.quote: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם יִרְחַק חֹק זְמַנּוֹ יַאֲרִיךְ וְלֹא יָבֹא לְעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says, in the enemy's words, that day's set time will stretch on and never come.

sources.quote: יוֹם הַהוּא יִרְחַק וִיבַטֵּל מֵעֲלֵיכֶם חֹק גְּזֵרוֹת הַבַּבְלִיִּים וּפַרְסִיִּים
sources.says: Rashi says that day will remove the decrees of the Babylonians and Persians from you.

sources.quote: אז ירחק חק המס, שהיית נותנת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says then the tax you used to pay will be removed.

sources.quote: חק. קצב של הזמן
sources.says: Malbim says חק means a fixed measure of time.

7:12.headline: מצור: fortified cities, or Egypt
7:12.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read מצור as a fortress. Others cited by Radak, and Malbim, read it here as a name for Egypt, as in "the rivers of מצור" (Isaiah 19:6).

sources.quote: ערי מצור. כמו ערי מבצר
sources.says: Radak says ערי מצור means fortified cities.

sources.quote: מצור. ענין מבצר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מצור means a fortress.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים ולמני מצור כמו מצרים
sources.says: Radak says some explain ולמני מצור as Egypt.

sources.quote: ולמני מצור היינו הגלות אשר בארץ מצרים
sources.says: Malbim says ולמני מצור means the exiles in the land of Egypt.

7:17.headline: זוחלי ארץ: creatures that glide like water, or that people fear
7:17.body: Metzudat Zion ties the word to flowing water: a snake has no legs and seems to stream along. Ibn Ezra ties it to Job 32:6, "I was afraid" (זחלתי): creeping things that frighten people.

sources.quote: ויקרא הנחש כן לפי שאין לו רגלים והלוכו נראה כזוחל ונגרר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the snake is called this because it has no legs and its movement looks like flowing and dragging.

sources.quote: הרמשים שיפחדו בני אדם מהם, כדרך האמים מגזרת זחלתי ואירא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are creeping things that people fear, from "I was afraid" (זחלתי).

sources.quote: הֵם נְחָשִׁים הַזּוֹחֲלִים עַל גְּחוֹנָם
sources.says: Rashi says they are snakes that crawl on their bellies.

7:18.headline: נשא עון: God carries the sin, or lifts it away
7:18.body: Metzudat Zion reads נשא as forgiving, and Radak pictures lifting a thing out of its place. Malbim says it means carrying: God bears the sin like a load, which is less than pressing it down or passing over it.

sources.quote: נושא. ענין מחילה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נושא means forgiveness.

sources.quote: נושא. כאדם שמסלק דבר ממקומו
sources.says: Radak says נושא is like a man removing something from its place.

sources.quote: נשא. משתתף עם נשיאת משא שסובל את העון
sources.says: Malbim says נשא shares its meaning with carrying a load: God bears the sin.

sources.quote: והכובש עון יכניע את העון בל יתרומם ולא יהיה למשא עליו
sources.says: Malbim says one who presses down sin subdues it so it no longer rises or weighs on him.

7:19.headline: God will press our sins down, so they no longer rule us
7:19.body: Radak pictures a man pressing something under his feet so it is not seen. Ibn Ezra says it reverses "sins overpowered me" (Psalms 65:4): now the sins will not rule over us.

sources.quote: יכבוש כאדם שכובש דבר תחת רגליו שלא יראה
sources.says: Radak says it is like a man who presses something under his feet so it will not be seen.

sources.quote: וטעם יכבוש הפוך דברי עונות גברו מני, שלא ימשלו בנו עוד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יכבוש is the reverse of "sins overpowered me": they will no longer rule over us.

sources.quote: יכבוש. ענין תפישה בחזקה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יכבוש means seizing by force.

7:20.headline: Why Jacob gets "truth" and Abraham gets "kindness"
7:20.body: Radak and Malbim explain the pairing. The land was a free gift to Abraham, so it is kindness. To Jacob it was already promised, so keeping it is truth. Ibn Ezra adds that Isaac is left out because he was also Edom's father.

sources.quote: החסד הוא לאברהם שנתן לו בחסדו הארץ ולבניו אחריו
sources.says: Radak says the kindness is to Abraham, to whom God gave the land in kindness, and to his children after him.

sources.quote: האמת הוא לקיים המתנה לבניו
sources.says: Radak says the truth is keeping that gift for Jacob's children.

sources.quote: שאל אברהם לא נתחייב עדיין מצד הבטחה קודמת ונקרא חסד
sources.says: Malbim says God owed Abraham nothing from an earlier promise, so it is called kindness.

sources.quote: ולא הזכיר יצחק, כי גם הוא אבי אדום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Isaac is not mentioned because he is also the father of Edom.
